acceptedAnswer.text: SUAY is an open-source project for local AI resource sharing. It provides an organization access and inference-gateway pilot, alongside a separate experimental Petals LAN compute pool.

name: Can old computers run AI together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some older machines can contribute if their supported runtime, memory and network meet the workload requirements. SUAY does not guarantee that every old device can run a model or improve performance.

name: Does SUAY combine the RAM of every device?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Petals experiment distributes supported model blocks across workers. It is not a general shared-memory system. A request-routing inference pool and splitting one large model are different approaches.

The pilot includes user roles, zone and selected-node visibility, expiring API keys, request budgets, audit events and an inference proxy to an approved backend. Worker commands remain pending until native transport is implemented.

The Python control-plane pilot can be evaluated where its dependencies run. The compute pilot needs a verified Petals environment. Native Windows, macOS and Linux service installers are planned; Android compute is not a released feature.

name: Is SUAY free for business use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Original SUAY code is MIT licensed and can be used commercially under that license. Model weights and dependencies have separate terms; BLOOM uses BigScience RAIL. Review each model before organizational use.

name: Can developers use SUAY through an API?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An operator can configure an approved inference backend and issue scoped API keys for non-streaming chat completions. Budgets count accepted requests; reported model-token usage is tracked separately.
SUAY is an early pilot. Native worker identity, SSO/MFA, signed deployment and automatic model migration are not complete. Evaluate it on a trusted test network before considering production.

name: Which machine is the SUAY coordinator?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Petals LAN pilot, every compute machine runs the same auto_agent.py. The lowest active IPv4 becomes coordinator and also serves model blocks. The organization gateway on port 8090 is a separate pilot.

name: How do I start a SUAY worker?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a dedicated Petals Python 3.10 environment on a supported Linux host, install agent requirements, configure its LAN IP and shared model settings, then run versions/python/compute/agent/auto_agent.py. Check port 8080 and actual model block coverage before starting a client.

name: Does the SUAY client include a web AI chat?

acceptedAnswer.text: The current Petals client is a terminal application. Run versions/python/compute/client/app.py with --coordinator http://AGENT_IP:8080 after agents are ready. The AI Agent web window in the GIF is an illustration, not a released chat UI.

name: Does installing the SUAY gateway install an AI model?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The organization dashboard and inference gateway manage access and forward requests. An operator must configure a separately running OpenAI-compatible inference backend. The gateway is not automatically connected to the Petals LAN pool.
